title: harnessed recipe
description: A composable capability bundle added ONTO an agent (catalog/recipes/<name>/recipe.yaml, or catalog/recipes/<family>/<variety>/recipe.yaml for one variety of a recipe family — referenced from a stack as `<family>/<variety>`). Harness-independent — no `harnesses:` field; harness-specific build steps branch on ${HARNESS} inside the recipe's Dockerfile. Carries metadata only; build steps live in the Dockerfile. See docs/harnessed-design.md §7/§11.

description.description: Human-readable summary of what this recipe contributes.

mcp.description: MCP layer: server entries merged into the stack's hatago config across all recipes.

skills.description: Standalone skill dirs shipped by this recipe (Claude-canonical), fanned into the profile's .claude/skills/. Each entry is a path relative to the recipe dir.

commands.description: Standalone command dirs shipped by this recipe (Claude-canonical), fanned into the profile's .claude/commands/. Each entry is a path relative to the recipe dir.

rules.description: Standalone rule dirs shipped by this recipe (Claude-canonical), fanned into the profile's .claude/rules/. Each entry is a path relative to the recipe dir.

expect.description: Smoke-check subset the capability test probes after building — for capabilities delivered via the recipe's Dockerfile (which the assembler cannot infer by parsing). Not a completeness oracle.

mcp.description: MCP server names expected connected through the hatago hub.

egress.description: Extra outbound hosts this recipe's tools need, appended to the container egress firewall allowlist (catalog/base/egress-firewall.sh) at launch — ONLY when this recipe is in the stack (default-DROP otherwise). Bare hostnames: no scheme, path, or port (e.g. 'api.pulumi.com'). See docs/guides/egress.md.

tools.description: Pinned mise tools installed into the derived image as a `mise use -g` layer, letting a recipe add a CLI with no Dockerfile (e.g. 'pulumi@3.140.0'). MUST be pinned — a floating '@latest' or bare tool name is rejected. Accepts any mise spec: registered tool, github:owner/repo@tag, or npm:pkg@version. An entry may instead be a {spec, hold} mapping, where a non-empty `hold` reason marks that one pin manual-upgrade-only for `harnessed update`; the pin is still installed identically. See docs/guides/egress.md.

spec.description: The pinned mise tool spec, exactly as it would be written in the plain string form.

hold.description: Non-empty reason this ONE pin is manual-upgrade-only. `harnessed update` lists it informationally, never offers it for bumping, and never fails `--check` on it. A hold does not license a floating ref — the spec must still be pinned.

env.description: Environment variables set for the RUNNING agent (and its hooks and child processes) — the one recipe deliverable a script cannot provide, since a script's `export` dies with the script. Delivered as image ENV at build, as `podman run -e` on the container, and into the launcher's own environment on `launch --host`. Values are mode-portable TEMPLATES, not literals: `{persist:<name>}` resolves to wherever this recipe's persist entry <name> actually lives in the current mode (the container bind-mount target vs. the real host persist dir), `{project_dir}` to the workspace root, `{host_home}` to the real host $HOME. Do NOT hardcode a container-absolute path like /home/harnessed/... — it does not exist on a host launch. Distinct from mcp.servers[].env, which is per-MCP-server.

plugins.description: Vendored Claude plugins (forward field, design §11). Either a marketplace+plugin reference or a url+sha[+subdir] reference.

hooks.description: Declarative Claude Code hooks (GAP 2), merged by the assembler into the profile's settings.json. Maps event name to a list of {command, matcher?} entries, plus the optional non-event key `skip_harnesses`. `command` must already exist in the image (baked by this recipe's Dockerfile) — Claude Code's own hook runner invokes it inside the instance; this is NOT the host-side `init:` mechanism (which runs once, before the agent attaches). See docs/todos/2026-06-27-recipe-stress-test.md GAP 2.

skip_harnesses.description: Harnesses on which THIS recipe's hooks are NOT emitted. For a capability delivered NATIVELY on that harness, where replaying the same hooks would double-fire (e.g. context-mode installs upstream's own omp plugin, so its hooks must not also be replayed through omp-claude-hooks-bridge). Drops only the declaring recipe's entries, only on the listed harnesses — other recipes' hooks in the same stack are untouched. Recipes stay harness-independent otherwise: harness-specific BUILD steps branch on ${HARNESS} in the Dockerfile, but hooks are not a build step and so cannot use that escape hatch.

command.description: Shell command Claude Code runs when this event fires.

matcher.description: Optional matcher (tool name for PreToolUse/PostToolUse; "startup"|"resume"|"clear" for SessionStart, etc). Ignored by events that don't support matching.

setup.description: Harness-agnostic manual-setup note. USER-FACING: shown host-side by the launcher at attach time (an interactive [O]k/[D]ismiss/[Q]uit prompt), NEVER baked into any agent identity/rules file. Use when the recipe's tool needs a one-time manual step (account, API key, CLI init) that harnessed can't or shouldn't automate. Omit entirely when the recipe is self-contained.

summary.description: One-line, harness-agnostic setup note (what the user needs to do).

reference.description: Upstream docs/GitHub URL the user can consult for details.

condition.description: Optional shell command that exits 0 when the manual step is STILL needed (e.g. `! mytool status`). Evaluated host-side in the project directory on every launch: exit 0 shows the notice, non-zero (satisfied) suppresses it. A recipe with no condition shows once per project until the user dismisses it; the dismiss flag gates only unconditional notices, conditional ones always follow their condition.

run.description: Executable first-run setup command (host-native `launch --host`). Resolved with repo-identity primitives ({repo}, {gcd_db}, …) and {config.<key>} values, then run once when `condition` is satisfied. Use for setup harnessed CAN automate (e.g. `mytool init --database {config.database}`).

script.description: Path (relative to the recipe dir) of a bash script run in BOTH host and container mode — the both-mode replacement for `run` and for `provision:`. Mutually exclusive with `run`. Unlike `run` it is a FILE, so it cannot be templated: every input arrives as env instead (HARNESSED_MODE, HARNESSED_STACK, HARNESSED_PROJECT_DIR, HARNESSED_HOST_HOME, HARNESSED_BIN_DIR, the repo-identity primitives as HARNESSED_REPO/_GCD_DB/_GCD_HASH/_PROJECT_HASH, and each `config` key as HARNESSED_CFG_<KEY>). Runs on every launch, so it MUST be idempotent and self-gating. Host mode: run by the launcher with HARNESSED_BIN_DIR leading PATH, so it can install a tool then immediately configure it. Container mode: mounted read-only and run via `podman exec` after start and before the egress firewall closes, with the same vars set as real container env.

confirm.description: Warning the user must accept BEFORE `run`/`script` executes. Declare it when the setup's side effects land in the USER'S repo rather than in harnessed's own state — e.g. a first-run init that creates and COMMITS files into a shared checkout. The launcher prints this text, requires an explicit yes, and NEVER runs the setup without a TTY (a headless launch cannot consent). Declining skips only that launch; `condition` brings the offer back next time, and the confirm is not even shown when `condition` reports the work is already done. Meaningless without `run` or `script`, and rejected on its own.

config.description: Config values `run`/`script` needs, resolved on first launch. Each is either derived (silent, from repo-identity primitives) or prompted (asked once; non-interactive uses the default). Referenced in `run` as {config.<key>}, and exposed to `script` as HARNESSED_CFG_<KEY>.

derive.description: Template over repo-identity primitives ({repo}, {gcd_db}, {gcd_hash}). Resolved silently.

prompt.description: Question asked on first launch (templated). Non-interactive → uses default.

install.description: Build-phase install script — ONE bash file executed by BOTH the container build (`RUN bash <script>` in the derived Dockerfile) and a host launch, replacing a container-only Dockerfile RUN. Differs from `setup.script` ONLY in phase: install runs at BUILD time container-side and immediately after the host home is materialized host-side; setup runs at container RUNTIME and after install host-side. Because a build has no project bind-mount, the install env is deliberately a SUBSET of the folder-env contract: HARNESS, HARNESSED_MODE, HARNESSED_RECIPE_DIR, HARNESSED_CONFIG_DIR (the agent config dir to install into), HARNESSED_INSTALL_CACHE — and no PROJECT_DIR. Anything needing project context belongs in `setup.script`. These harnessed-owned vars win over the recipe's own `env:` in both modes. The script runs on EVERY host launch (the host home is rebuilt from scratch each time) so it must be idempotent.

script.description: Path (relative to the recipe dir) of the bash install script. Linted like a Dockerfile body: raw npm/npx and floating refs are rejected. Optional ONLY for a ROOT-ONLY install, which has no user-level half: then `system` alone is declared, the step stays in the recipe Dockerfile, and the host executor's sole job is to warn.

cache.description: PINNED content ref (tag/version/SHA) keying the host content cache at $XDG_CACHE_HOME/harnessed/install/<recipe>/<cache>, handed to the script as $HARNESSED_INSTALL_CACHE (empty when omitted). Cache MISS is 'the directory does not exist' — harnessed creates only its parent; the script populates it and copies out of it. This is what makes the mandatory per-launch re-run affordable. Floating values (latest/main/master/HEAD/...) are rejected: a moving key never refreshes. Keep it equal to the ref pinned inside the script.

refs.description: Declared upstream refs for a CONTENT install (D1a). The pin is DATA and lives here so `harnessed update` has ONE place to look; the fetch stays in install.sh, because the real Family B installs differ too much to declare without inventing a DSL. Each key maps to HARNESSED_REF_<KEY> and HARNESSED_REPO_<KEY> in the install env. When present, `install.cache` is DERIVED from these (refs sorted by key, each rendered `key=repo@ref`, newline-joined with no trailing newline, UTF-8 SHA-256, first 16 lowercase hex) and declaring `cache:` as well is an error, not a precedence rule.

repo.description: `owner/repo` — what `update` queries. NOT a URL: install.sh composes the URL, so switching from a git clone to a tarball fetch needs no manifest change.

ref.description: A version tag or a FULL 40-character commit SHA. Floating refs are rejected exactly as they are for `tools:`; an abbreviated SHA is not a stable identifier.

hold.description: Non-empty reason string ⇒ THIS ref is manual-upgrade-only. Scope is the single ref, so a recipe with three refs may hold one and auto-bump two. A hold never licenses a floating ref.

system.description: Set to a non-empty reason string when this recipe's install has a SYSTEM-LEVEL component (USER root, apt-get, COPY into /usr/local/bin) that only a container build can perform — that part stays in the recipe Dockerfile. harnessed never sudos or mutates the user's system, so on a host launch the component is skipped and this string is printed verbatim as a loud warning naming the recipe. Declaring it is what keeps the skip from being SILENT.

hold.description: Set to a non-empty reason string when every pin fetched BY this install script is MANUAL-UPGRADE-ONLY. `harnessed update` may list a newer upstream ref for them, but never offers them in the interactive bump set and never fails `--check` on them. The motivating case is SKILL content: a skill is agent INSTRUCTIONS run with the agent's full tool permissions, so a compromised upgrade is prompt injection rather than a CVE — no osv/trivy/grype-class scanner detects it and a human must read the diff. `cache` cannot carry this meaning: a cache key can be used for any CLI+content combination, so its presence classifies nothing. Like `system`, the value is a REASON shown to whoever decides whether to lift the hold, not a flag. Per-tool equivalent: the `{spec, hold}` mapping form of `tools`.

deps.description: Dependency declarations (forward field, design §11). Usually auto-detected from a vendored plugin; declare here for standalone recipes/overrides. uv for Python, pnpm for Node (never npm/npx).

python.description: requirements.txt → `uv pip install -r`; pyproject.toml → `uv venv` + `uv pip install -e .`.

scripts.description: Build/setup script command strings (forward field, design §11). Scanned by the supply-chain lint (no raw npm/npx — use pnpm dlx).

conflicts.description: Names of other recipes this recipe must never be combined with in the same stack (e.g. two recipes that both claim to be the agent's sole cross-session memory store). Checked symmetrically across a stack's recipe list — declaring it on either side is enough. Do NOT list sibling varieties of the same family here: two varieties of one recipe (`<family>/<a>` + `<family>/<b>`) are ALREADY implicitly exclusive.

services.description: Sidecar services this recipe requires that have no MCP surface (e.g. a database server speaking its own wire protocol). Unioned with the stack's own services: at launch.

persist.description: Folders/files that must survive harnessed's --fresh launches. A LIST of entries; each declares scope + location explicitly (never inferred from the string shape). See docs/guides/recipe-authoring.md.

init.description: Per-project setup sourced in the attach shell (Model A): `run` is executed inline in the shell that then starts the harness, so any env it exports (e.g. BEADS_DIR) reaches the agent. Runs on EVERY launch/attach, so `run` MUST self-gate (idempotent) — there is no host-side marker. Contract env vars available to `run`: PROJECT_DIR, MAIN_REPO_DIR, CONTAINER_WORKSPACE_DIR, HOST_WORKSPACE_DIR. See docs/guides/recipe-authoring.md.

run.description: Shell command sourced in the attach shell on every launch. MUST self-gate cheaply (e.g. `mytool status >/dev/null 2>&1 || mytool init`); a non-zero exit aborts the attach before the harness starts. Use `return`/short-circuits, never a bare `exit`. No secrets are available.

persistEntry.description: One persist entry. scope: global bind-mounts a real host `path` as-is; scope: workspace|project stores a `name` (host-managed or in_repo). location: in_repo requires `vcs`.

scope.description: workspace (per launch path) | project (per git-common-dir, shared across worktrees) | global (a real host path).

location.description: host (harnessed-managed dir bind-mounted at ~/<name>) | in_repo (inside the mounted workspace). Omitted for scope: global.

name.description: $HOME-relative name (scope: workspace|project). Not used for scope: global.

path.description: Real host path to bind-mount as-is (scope: global only; must be in the persist allowlist).

vcs.description: tracked | ignored — git-tracking intent; REQUIRED for location: in_repo, invalid otherwise.

mcpServer.description: One MCP server. A stdio server (with `command`) is run by hatago as a child (stdio→HTTP). A network-native server (`url`/`service`, transport http) is proxied by hatago. `service` and `command` are mutually exclusive.

command.description: Executable for a stdio child server (e.g. uvx). Mutually exclusive with `service`. Never raw npm/npx — use pnpm dlx.

transport.description: Transport. 'stdio' (default) → hatago child; 'http' → Streamable-HTTP URL proxy. 'sse' is not supported (Streamable-HTTP MCP only).

url.description: Endpoint for a network-native server (transport http).

service.description: Reference to a shared service (services/<name>); the assembler resolves it to a hatago URL-proxy entry. Mutually exclusive with `command`.

url_env.description: Optional env var injected into the instance carrying the resolved URL.

headers.description: HTTP headers for a network-native server.

direct.description: Wire this server STRAIGHT into the harness config instead of proxying it through hatago. Mutually exclusive with the hub: a direct server is emitted into .mcp.json and left out of hatago.config.json, so it is reachable by exactly one route. Requires `url` (or `url_env`) and is incompatible with `service`. What it buys, for a server the harness can already speak to: the harness owns the connection, so an OAuth flow is the harness's own and its authorize URL renders in the harness UI, instead of landing on the stderr of hatago's child where nothing reads it. What it costs: hatago's curation does not apply — no tool filtering, no per-server instructions, description or tags — so the harness sees the server's full surface, unannotated. Honoured only by harnesses whose MCP config harnessed emits (claude); codex and omp bake theirs into the image, so declaring it for them is a build-time error.

oauth.description: OAuth settings for a `direct` server. Only meaningful with `direct: true` — a hub child's callback port is its own argument, read from `args`.

callback_port.description: Fixed port for the OAuth redirect, emitted as `oauth.callbackPort`. PINNED deliberately: the launcher must publish this port on the pod BEFORE the harness starts, so a runtime-chosen port can never be forwarded and the redirect dies in a netns the browser cannot reach. Floor is 1024 because the pod is rootless and cannot publish a privileged port.

allOf.description: A direct server is addressed by URL over Streamable-HTTP, so it must say so and must have somewhere to connect. An omitted transport would default to stdio and emit `type: "stdio"` beside a URL — a config that parses and a server that never connects.

fileExt.description: A standalone skill/command dir: a bare path string, or { path: ... }.

plugin.description: A vendored Claude plugin reference: marketplace+plugin, or url+sha[+subdir].
